full_sentence: You may have noticed that there has been a rise in the number of beauty brands launching these refillable products.

Beauty companies all seem to follow the same strategy: cheaper brands like Dove, as well as more expensive brands, luxury players like Chanel, they all seem to have jumped on the refillable bandwagon.
Obviously, the cosmetics industry has to follow suit, or otherwise it would have an image problem.
Hence the wave of refillable products, because, as I've mentioned before, using refills generates less waste than buying the primary packaging over and over again.
So those refillable products look like an easy win for the planet — but looks can be deceiving.
It begs the question: how many beauty products have you repurchased more than 50 times?
A huge number of beauty products are destroyed each year by manufacturers and retailers without ever hitting the market.
In summary, sustainability in the beauty industry is a complex journey.
Refillable may not be the answer to all problems, in fact, it may well be just another buzzword, but at least it raises awareness, which I suppose is key in bringing about true change.
